title: Faster OAuth Errors & Clearer OAuth Guidance for Agents

Improved: OAuth 2.0 sign-in now checks the authorization URL first and shows an error straight away when the server is unreachable or rejects the request, instead of waiting 120 seconds.
The agent skill now explains how to tell which OAuth 2.0 grant a server offers, and when to use each one.
The agent skill now says when to use OAuth 1.0a, and which OAuth grants are not supported.
The agent skill now explains that all OAuth blocks in a file share one sign-in.
Fixed: A cancelled or finished OAuth sign-in can no longer end a newer one when its timer runs out.
The agent skill no longer suggests placing the auth block inside the request block.
The agent skill now tells agents to use Voiden's own callback address, never a page on the API server.

title: Headless Auth Fix & OAuth Guidance for Agents

Fixed: Bearer, Basic, and API key auth now send their credentials when run headlessly (voiden-runner, voiden-mcp), instead of empty values.
Basic auth now resolves {{VARIABLES}} in the username and password when run headlessly.
The agent skill's OAuth 2.0 examples now use valid client authentication values.
Improved: The agent skill now explains when to use an OAuth 2.0 block and when not to, such as cookie-based logins.
The agent skill now documents OAuth 2.0 callback URLs, automatic PKCE, token variables, and a token-request pattern for headless runs.

title: Docs: Skill Now Documents the Single Auth Slot Rule

Fixed: The bundled skill.md now documents that all auth types (bearer, basic, apiKey, oauth1, oauth2, digest, awsSignature, ntlm, hawk, netrc, atlassianAsap, inherit/none) share one single auth block per request section. This was previously undocumented, which could lead an AI agent to insert a second auth block instead of editing the existing one when asked to change auth type.

title: Headless Auth Now Actually Applies & Inline Block Help

Added: The Auth block now shows an inline "?" help tooltip in its header, matching the other request blocks
Fixed: The Auth block (Bearer, Basic, API Key) is now parsed and actually applied as request headers/query params when running headlessly via the CLI or voiden-mcp — previously nothing in the headless request-build pipeline read the auth block at all, so every CLI/MCP request silently ran with no authentication regardless of what was configured in the Auth tab, while the real Voiden app's Send button (which applies auth in the renderer before the request ever leaves it) was never affected

Merges its auth-derived headers/query params with whatever another plugin's request-build handler already contributed (e.g. voiden-rest-api's headers-table rows) instead of overwriting them, regardless of which plugin's handler runs first

title: Block Documentation Link & Auth Table Cell Borders

Added: An "Open Documentation" item now appears in the Auth block's right-click block menu, opening the Voiden Blocks docs in your system browser
Fixed: Auth block now shows the same bordered card and cell grid as other request tables (Headers, Query Params, etc.) — every auth type's fields (Basic, Bearer, API Key, OAuth 2.0, and the rest) were previously borderless, making cells hard to tell apart, especially in low-contrast themes

title: Copy/Paste as cURL Auth Fixes & Skill Documentation Expansion

Added: Pasting a cURL command now builds the matching auth block: Basic, Digest, NTLM, AWS Signature, and Bearer are fully reconstructed; OAuth 1.0 is fully reconstructed when signed PLAINTEXT (consumer/token secrets are recoverable from the signature) or partially reconstructed with a warning for HMAC-signed requests (secrets aren't recoverable from a one-way signature); Hawk recovers the id with a warning that the key must be re-entered; Netrc shows a warning instead of a block, since machine/login/password live in ~/.netrc rather than the pasted command
Fixed: Copy as cURL now includes Digest, NTLM, AWS Signature, Netrc, and OAuth 1.0 (PLAINTEXT) auth — a fragile dynamic import used to reach the cURL header extender registry and was silently dropping every one of these auth types from the generated command with no error surfaced anywhere; registration and lookup now go through a direct context reference instead
Copy as cURL no longer repeats the same auth flags multiple times in the generated command

Netrc auth in Copy as cURL now includes the actual login/password via -u instead of a bare --netrc flag, which only works if the machine running the command happens to already have a matching ~/.netrc entry
OAuth 2.0 auth in Copy as cURL now embeds the actual resolved access token instead of an unresolved {{process.*}} placeholder, which has no meaning outside Voiden
Copy as cURL now surfaces a warning toast for Hawk and Atlassian ASAP auth, which require a live-computed signature/JWT with no static cURL representation, instead of silently omitting them
Improved: AI skill documentation significantly expanded with full OAuth2 configuration reference (all grant types, PKCE, token fields), complete auth block attr schemas, and Atlassian ASAP auth method documentation

Added: Plugin API for extending cURL output — plugins can register a `registerCurlHeaderExtender` function to inject headers, query params, or raw cURL flags into the cURL command produced by CopyCurlButton
Fixed: Remove catch-all shim from build pipeline for correct dependency bundling

Added: Block outline metadata for the auth block so it displays at its correct document position in the Block Overview Panel, with the auth type (Bearer Token, OAuth 2.0, etc.) shown as the preview
Fixed: OAuth2 auto-acquire and auto-refresh now show toast with specific error when config fields are missing or token server returns error

title: SDK v2 Migration
description: Rewritten on the new SDK pipeline architecture with improved OAuth2 support.

Added: OAuth2 Client Credentials, Authorization Code, and Password flows
Improved: Bearer token block redesigned with token preview
Basic auth now encodes correctly for all character sets
